readings.title: Amatsyahu Ascends in Yehuḏah
readings.subtitle: Partial Adherence to the Master Architecture
readings.text: [2 Kings 14:1] In the second year of Yo’ash son of Yo’aḥaz, sovereign of Yisra’ěl, Amatsyahu son of Yo’ash, sovereign of Yehuḏah, began to reign. [2] He was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Yerushalayim. And his mother’s name was Yeho‛addin of Yerushalayim. [3] And he did what was right in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, but not like his father Daviḏ. He did according to all his father Yo’ash did. [4] However, the high places were not taken away. The people still slaughtered and burned incense on the high places.

readings.title: Execution of the Conspirators
readings.subtitle: Strict Adherence to the Torah of Individual Accountability
readings.text: [5] And it came to be, as soon as the reign was strengthened in his hand, that he struck <dn>את</dn> his servants who had stricken <dn>את</dn> his father the sovereign. [6] But he did not put to death the children of the strikers, according to what is written in the Book of the Torah of Mosheh, in which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> commanded, saying, <dq>Fathers are not put to death for the children, and children are not put to death for the fathers, but each one is put to death for his own sin.</dq>

readings.title: The Conquest of Sela
readings.subtitle: Establishing Dominance over Eḏom
readings.text: [7] He struck <dn>את</dn> Eḏom in the Valley of Salt, ten thousand, and took <dn>את</dn> Sela in battle, and called its name Yoqthe’ěl to this day.

readings.title: The Thistle and the Cedar
readings.subtitle: Yeho’ash Rebukes the Pride of Amatsyahu
readings.text: [2 Kings 14:8] Amatsyah then sent messengers to Yeho’ash son of Yeho’aḥaz, son of Yěhu, sovereign of Yisra’ěl, saying, “Come, let us look each other in the face!” [9] And Yeho’ash sovereign of Yisra’ěl sent to Amatsyahu sovereign of Yehuḏah, saying, “The thistle that was in Leḇanon sent to the cedar that was in Leḇanon, saying, ‘Give your daughter to my son as wife.’ And a wild beast that was in Leḇanon passed by and trampled the thistle. [10] “You have certainly stricken Eḏom, and your heart has lifted you up. Be esteemed and stay in your house. But why do you stir up yourself to evil, that you should fall – you and Yehuḏah with you?”

readings.title: The Breach of Yerushalayim
readings.subtitle: Yehuḏah Smitten and the Treasures Pillaged
readings.text: [11] But Amatsyahu did not listen, so Yeho’ash sovereign of Yisra’ěl went up, and he and Amatsyahu sovereign of Yehuḏah faced one another at Běyth Shemesh, which belongs to Yehuḏah. [12] And Yehuḏah was smitten before Yisra’ěl, and they each fled to his tent. [13] And Yeho’ash sovereign of Yisra’ěl caught <dn>את</dn> Amatsyahu sovereign of Yehuḏah, son of Yeho’ash, son of Aḥazyahu, at Běyth Shemesh. And they came to Yerushalayim and he broke through <dn>את</dn> the wall of Yerushalayim from the Gate of Ephrayim to the Corner Gate, four hundred cubits, [14] and took <dn>את</dn> all the gold and silver, and <dn>את</dn> all the objects that were found in the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and in <dn>את</dn> the treasuries of the sovereign’s house, and <dn>את</dn> hostages, and returned to Shomeron.

readings.title: Amatsyahu’s Reign and Justice
readings.subtitle: Establishing Strong Control Without a Perfect Heart
readings.text: [2 Chronicles 25:1] Amatsyahu was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Yerushalayim. And the name of his mother was Yehoaddan of Yerushalayim. [2] And he did what was right in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, but not with a perfect heart. [3] And it came to be, upon his strong control of the reign, that he killed <dn>את</dn> his servants who had struck <dn>את</dn> his father the sovereign. [4] But he did not put their children to death, but did as it is written in the Torah in the Book of Mosheh, where <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> commanded, saying, <dq>Fathers are not put to death for their children, and children are not put to death for their fathers, but each one has to die for his own sin.</dq>

readings.title: The Economic Test of Trust
readings.subtitle: Leaning on Emunah Over the Strength of Yisra’ěl
readings.text: [5] And Amatsyahu gathered <dn>את</dn> Yehuḏah and set over them commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds, according to the fathers’ houses, for all Yehuḏah and Binyamin. And he registered them from twenty years old and above, and found them to be three hundred thousand choice men going out to the army, handling spear and shield. [6] And he hired one hundred thousand mighty brave ones from Yisra’ěl for one hundred talents of silver. [7] But a man of <dn>Elohim</dn> came to him, saying, <dq>O sovereign, do not let the army of Yisra’ěl go with you, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is not with Yisra’ěl, with all the children of Ephrayim.</dq> [8] <dq>But if you are going, do it! Be strong in battle, else <dn>Elohim</dn> would make you fall before the enemy, for <dn>Elohim</dn> has power to help and to overthrow.</dq> [9] And Amatsyahu said to the man of <dn>Elohim</dn>, “But what do we do about the hundred talents which I have given to the army of Yisra’ěl?” And the man of <dn>Elohim</dn> answered, <dq><dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has more to give you than this.</dq> [10] So Amatsyahu dismissed the army that had come to him from Ephrayim, to go back home. And they were greatly enraged against Yehuḏah, and they returned home in a rage.

readings.title: Victory in the Valley of Salt
readings.subtitle: Retaliation from the Discarded Mercenaries
readings.text: [11] And Amatsyahu strengthened himself, and led his people, and went to the Valley of Salt and struck <dn>את</dn> ten thousand of the sons of Sě‛ir. [12] And the sons of Yehuḏah took captive <dn>את</dn> another ten thousand alive, and they brought them to the top of the rock, and threw them down from the top of the rock, and all of them were dashed to pieces. [13] And the soldiers of the army which Amatsyahu had sent back from going with him to battle, they raided the cities of Yehuḏah from Shomeron to Běyth Ḥoron, and struck <dn>את</dn> three thousand in them, and took <dn>את</dn> much spoil.

readings.title: The Snare of Assimilation
readings.subtitle: Amatsyahu Adopts the Mighty Ones of Sě‛ir
readings.text: [2 Chronicles 25:14] And it came to be, after Amatsyahu came from striking the Eḏomites, that he brought <dn>את</dn> the mighty ones of the people of Sě‛ir, and set them up to be his mighty ones, and bowed down before them and burned incense to them. [15] Therefore the displeasure of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> burned against Amatsyahu, and <dn>He</dn> sent him a prophet who said to him, <dq>Why have you sought the mighty ones of the people, which did not deliver <dn>את</dn> their own people from your hand?</dq> [16] And it came to be, as he talked with him, that the sovereign said to him, “Have we appointed you counsellor to the sovereign? Stop! Why should they strike you?” Then the prophet stopped and said, <dq>I know that <dn>Elohim</dn> has counselled to destroy you, because you have done this and have not listened to my counsel.</dq>

readings.title: The Ill-Fated Challenge
readings.subtitle: Yisra’ěl Answers the Arrogance of Yehuḏah
readings.text: [17] And Amatsyahu sovereign of Yehuḏah took counsel and sent to Yo’ash son of Yeho’aḥaz, son of Yěhu, sovereign of Yisra’ěl, saying, “Come, let us look each other in the face!” [18] And Yo’ash sovereign of Yisra’ěl sent to Amatsyahu sovereign of Yehuḏah, saying, “The thistle that was in Leḇanon sent to the cedar that was in Leḇanon, saying, ‘Give your daughter to my son as wife.’ And a wild beast that was in Leḇanon passed by and trampled the thistle. [19] “You have said, ‘See, I have stricken Eḏom,’ and your heart has lifted you up to boast. Now stay at home, why should you stir up yourself to evil, that you should fall – you and Yehuḏah with you?”

readings.title: Defeat Decreed by Elohim
readings.subtitle: The Wall Broken and the Hěḵal Spoiled
readings.text: [20] But Amatsyahu did not listen, for it came from <dn>Elohim</dn>, in order to give them into the hand of their enemies, because they had sought the mighty ones of Eḏom. [21] So Yo’ash sovereign of Yisra’ěl went out. And he and Amatsyahu sovereign of Yehuḏah faced one another at Běyth Shemesh, which belongs to Yehuḏah. [22] And Yehuḏah was smitten before Yisra’ěl, and they each fled to his tent. [23] And Yo’ash the sovereign of Yisra’ěl caught Amatsyahu sovereign of Yehuḏah, son of Yo’ash, son of Yeho’aḥaz, at Běyth Shemesh, and brought him to Yerushalayim, and broke down the wall of Yerushalayim from the Gate of Ephrayim to the Corner Gate, four hundred cubits, [24] and took <dn>את</dn> all the gold and the silver, and <dn>את</dn> all the utensils that were found in the House of <dn>Elohim</dn> with <dn>את</dn> Oḇěḏ-Eḏom, and <dn>את</dn> the treasures of the sovereign’s house, and <dn>את</dn> hostages, and returned to Shomeron.

readings.subsection: The Reign of Jehoash of Israel
readings.title: The Annals of Yo’ash
readings.subtitle: The End of an Era in Yisra’ěl
readings.text: [2 Kings 13:12] And the rest of the acts of Yo’ash, and all that he did, and his might with which he fought against Amatsyah sovereign of Yehuḏah, are they not written in the book of the annals of the sovereigns of Yisra’ěl? [13] So Yo’ash slept with his fathers. And Yaroḇ‛am sat on his throne. And Yo’ash was buried in Shomeron with the sovereigns of Yisra’ěl.

readings.subsection: The Reign of Jehoash of Israel
readings.title: The Succession in Shomeron
readings.subtitle: Yaroḇ‛am Ascends the Throne
readings.text: [2 Kings 14:15] And the rest of the acts of Yeho’ash which he did, and his might, and how he fought with Amatsyahu sovereign of Yehuḏah, are they not written in the book of the annals of the sovereigns of Yisra’ěl? [16] So Yeho’ash slept with his fathers, and was buried in Shomeron with the sovereigns of Yisra’ěl. And Yaroḇ‛am his son reigned in his place.

readings.subsection: The Reign of Jeroboam II of Israel
readings.title: The Expansion of Yisra’ěl
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH's Mercy Revealed Through Yonah's Prophecy
readings.text: [2 Kings 14:23] In the fifteenth year of Amatsyahu son of Yo’ash, the sovereign of Yehuḏah, Yaroḇ‛am son of Yo’ash, the sovereign of Yisra’ěl, began to reign in Shomeron, and reigned forty-one years. [24] And he did evil in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. He did not turn away from all the sins of Yaroḇ‛am son of Neḇat, who had made Yisra’ěl sin. [25] He restored <dn>את</dn> the border of Yisra’ěl from the entrance of Ḥamath to the Sea of the Araḇah, according to the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, which <dn>He</dn> had spoken through <dn>His</dn> servant Yonah son of Amittai, the prophet who was from Gath Ḥěpher. [26] For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> saw that the affliction of Yisra’ěl was very bitter. And there was no one, neither shut up nor left at large, to help Yisra’ěl. [27] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had not said that <dn>He</dn> would blot out <dn>את</dn> the name of Yisra’ěl from under the heavens, but saved them by the hand of Yaroḇ‛am son of Yo’ash.

readings.title: The Fall of Amatsyahu
readings.subtitle: Conspiracy and Death in Laḵish
readings.text: [2 Chronicles 25:25] And Amatsyahu son of Yo’ash, sovereign of Yehuḏah, lived fifteen years after the death of Yo’ash son of Yeho’aḥaz, sovereign of Yisra’ěl. [26] And the rest of the acts of Amatsyahu, from the first to the last, see, are they not written in the book of the sovereigns of Yehuḏah and Yisra’ěl? [27] And from the time that Amatsyahu turned away from following <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, they made a conspiracy against him in Yerushalayim, and he fled to Laḵish. And they sent after him to Laḵish and killed him there, [28] and they brought him on horses and buried him with his fathers in the City of Yehuḏah.

readings.title: The Final Years and Flight
readings.subtitle: Amatsyahu Buried in the City of Daviḏ
readings.text: [2 Kings 14:17] And Amatsyahu son of Yo’ash, sovereign of Yehuḏah, lived fifteen years after the death of Yeho’ash son of Yeho’aḥaz, sovereign of Yisra’ěl. [18] And the rest of the acts of Amatsyahu, are they not written in the book of the annals of the sovereigns of Yehuḏah? [19] And they made a conspiracy against him in Yerushalayim, and he fled to Laḵish. And they sent after him to Laḵish and killed him there, [20] and brought him on horses, and he was buried at Yerushalayim with his fathers in the City of Daviḏ.

readings.title: Azaryah Takes the Helm
readings.subtitle: The Restoration of Ěylath
readings.text: [21] And all the people of Yehuḏah took <dn>את</dn> Azaryah, who was sixteen years old, and set him up to reign instead of his father Amatsyahu. [22] He built <dn>את</dn> Ěylath and restored it to Yehuḏah, after the sovereign slept with his fathers.

readings.subsection: The Reign of Azariah (Uzziah) of Judah
readings.title: The Reign of Azaryah
readings.subtitle: Righteousness Mingled with Compromise
readings.text: [2 Kings 15:1] In the twenty-seventh year of Yaroḇ‛am sovereign of Yisra’ěl, Azaryah son of Amatsyah, sovereign of Yehuḏah, began to reign. [2] He was sixteen years old when he began to reign, and he reigned fifty-two years in Yerushalayim. And his mother’s name was Yeḵolyahu of Yerushalayim. [3] And he did what was right in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, according to all that his father Amatsyahu did, [4] however, the high places were not taken away. The people still slaughtered and burned incense on the high places.

readings.subsection: The Reign of Azariah (Uzziah) of Judah
readings.title: The Functional Consequence of Leprosy
readings.subtitle: The Sovereign Becomes Ritually Tame
readings.text: [5] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> smote <dn>את</dn> the sovereign, so that he was a leper until the day of his death, and he dwelt in a separate house. And Yotham son of the sovereign was over the house, ruling the people of the land.

readings.subsection: The Reign of Azariah (Uzziah) of Judah
readings.title: Uzziyahu’s Early Prosperity
readings.subtitle: Seeking Elohim in the Days of Zeḵaryahu
readings.text: [2 Chronicles 26:1] And all the people of Yehuḏah took <dn>את</dn> Uzziyahu, who was sixteen years old, and set him up to reign instead of his father Amatsyahu. [2] He built <dn>את</dn> Ěyloth and restored it to Yehuḏah, after the sovereign slept with his fathers. [3] Uzziyahu was sixteen years old when he began to reign, and he reigned fifty-two years in Yerushalayim. And his mother’s name was Yeḵolyah of Yerushalayim. [4] And he did what was right in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, according to all that his father Amatsyahu did. [5] And he sought <dn>Elohim</dn> in the days of Zeḵaryahu, who had understanding in the visions of <dn>Elohim</dn>. And while he sought <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dn>Elohim</dn> made him prosper.

readings.subsection: The Reign of Azariah (Uzziah) of Judah
readings.title: Military Might and Infrastructure
readings.subtitle: Breaking the Philistine Walls and Building Towers
readings.text: [6] And he went out and fought against the Philistines, and broke down <dn>את</dn> the wall of Gath, and <dn>את</dn> the wall of Yaḇneh, and <dn>את</dn> the wall of Ashdoḏ, and built cities around Ashdoḏ and among the Philistines. [7] And <dn>Elohim</dn> helped him against the Philistines, and against the Araḇians who lived in Gur Ba‛al, and the Me‛unites. [8] And the Ammonites gave gifts to Uzziyahu. And his name spread as far as the entrance of Mitsrayim, for he strengthened himself greatly. [9] And Uzziyahu built towers in Yerushalayim at the Corner Gate, and at the Valley Gate, and at the corner buttress, and strengthened them. [10] And he built towers in the wilderness, and dug many wells, for he had much livestock, both in the low country and in the plain, farmers and vinedressers in the mountains and in Karmel, for he loved the soil.

readings.subsection: The Reign of Azariah (Uzziah) of Judah
readings.title: The Master Architects of War
readings.subtitle: Machines and Shields for the Defense of Yerushalayim
readings.text: [11] And Uzziyah had an army of fighting men who went out to battle by divisions, according to the number on their roll as prepared by Ye‛i’ěl the scribe and Ma‛asěyahu the officer, under the hand of Ḥananyahu, one of the sovereign’s commanders. [12] The total number of the clan chiefs of the mighty brave ones was two thousand six hundred. [13] And under their hand was an army of three hundred and seven thousand five hundred that fought with mighty power, to help the sovereign against the enemy. [14] And Uzziyahu prepared for them, for the entire army, shields, and spears, and helmets, and body armour, and bows, and sling stones. [15] And he made machines in Yerushalayim, devised by skilled men, to be on the towers and the corners, to shoot arrows and large stones. And his name spread far and wide, for he was marvellously helped till he became strong.

readings.subsection: The Reign of Azariah (Uzziah) of Judah
readings.title: Usurping the Qadosh Office
readings.subtitle: Uzziyahu Violates the Boundaries of Authority
readings.text: [2 Chronicles 26:16] But when he became strong his heart was lifted up, to his destruction, for he trespassed against <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> his <dn>Elohim</dn> by entering the Hěḵal of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> to burn incense on the slaughter-place of incense. [17] And Azaryahu the priest went in after him, and with him were eighty priests of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, who were brave men. [18] And they stood up against Sovereign Uzziyahu, and said to him, “It is not for you, Uzziyahu, to burn incense to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, but for the priests, the sons of Aharon, who are set-apart to burn incense. Get out of the set-apart place, for you have trespassed, and there is no esteem to you from <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn>.”

readings.subsection: The Reign of Azariah (Uzziah) of Judah
readings.title: The Immediate Judgment
readings.subtitle: Leprosy in the House of YeHoVaH
readings.text: [19] And Uzziyahu was wroth. And he had a censer in his hand to burn incense. And while he was wroth with the priests, leprosy broke out on his forehead, before the priests in the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, beside the incense slaughter-place. [20] And Azaryahu the chief priest and all the priests looked at him, and saw that he was leprous on his forehead. And they hurried him from there. And he also hurried to get out, because <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had struck him. [21] And Sovereign Uzziyahu was a leper until the day of his death, and dwelt in a separate house, because he was a leper, for he was cut off from the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And Yotham his son was over the sovereign’s house, ruling the people of the land.

readings.title: The Commission to Ninevěh
readings.subtitle: Yonah Flees the Presence of YeHoVaH
readings.text: [Jonah 1:1] And the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to Yonah son of Amittai, saying, [2] <dq>Arise, go to Ninevěh, the great city, and cry out against it, for their evils have come up before <dn>Me</dn>.</dq> [3] But Yonah rose up to flee to Tarshish from the presence of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and went down to Yapho, and found a ship going to Tarshish. And he paid the fare, and went down into it, to go with them to Tarshish from the presence of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.

readings.title: The Tempest on the Sea
readings.subtitle: The Lots Fall Upon the Hebrew
readings.text: [4] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> sent out a great wind on the sea, and there was a great storm on the sea, so that the ship was thought to be broken up. [5] And the seamen were afraid, and each one cried out to his mighty one, and threw <dn>את</dn> the cargo which was in the ship into the sea, to lighten the load. But Yonah had gone down into the lowest parts of the ship, and he lay down, and was fast asleep. [6] And the captain came to him, and said to him, “What do you mean, sleeper? Arise, cry out to your <dn>Elohim</dn>, if so be that <dn>Elohim</dn> shall think about us, so that we do not perish.” [7] And they said to each other, “Come, and let us cast lots, so that we know for whose sake this evil has come upon us.” So they cast lots, and the lot fell on Yonah. [8] So they said to him, “Please explain to us! For whose sake is this evil upon us? What is your occupation? And where do you come from? What is your country? And from what people are you?” [9] And he said to them, <dq>I am a Hebrew. And <dn>I</dn> am fearing <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of the heavens, who made <dn>את</dn> the sea and the dry land.</dq> [10] And the men were exceedingly afraid, and said to him, “Why have you done this?” For the men knew that he fled from the presence of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, for he had informed them.

readings.title: A Life for a Calm Sea
readings.subtitle: The Seamen Fear the Creator of the Dry Land
readings.text: [11] And they said to him, “What are we to do to you to make the sea calm for us?” For the sea was growing more stormy. [12] And he said to them, “Take me and throw me into the sea, so that the sea becomes calm for you. For I know that this great storm is because of me.” [13] However, the men rowed hard to bring the ship to land, but were unable, for the sea continued to grow more stormy against them. [14] And they cried out to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and said, <dq>We pray, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, please, let us not perish for this man’s life, and do not lay on us innocent blood. For <dn>You</dn>, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, have done as it pleased <dn>You</dn>.</dq> [15] Then they took <dn>את</dn> Yonah and threw him into the sea, and the sea stopped raging. [16] And the men feared <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> exceedingly, and slaughtered a slaughtering to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and made vows.

readings.title: The Prophetic Crucible
readings.subtitle: The Sign of the Messiah Authenticated in the Deep
readings.text: [Jonah 1:17] But <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> appointed a great fish to swallow <dn>את</dn> Yonah. And Yonah was in the stomach of the fish three days and three nights.

readings.title: The Prayer from She’ol
readings.subtitle: Remembering YeHoVaH from the Heart of the Seas
readings.text: [Jonah 2:1] And Yonah prayed to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> his <dn>Elohim</dn> from the stomach of the fish. [2] And he said, <dq>I called to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> because of my distress, and <dn>He</dn> answered me. From the stomach of She’ol <dn>I</dn> cried, and <dn>You</dn> heard my voice.</dq> [3] <dq>For <dn>You</dn> threw me into the deep, into the heart of the seas, and the floods surrounded me. All <dn>Your</dn> breakers and <dn>Your</dn> waves passed over me.</dq> [4] <dq>So <dn>I</dn> said, ‘<dn>I</dn> have been driven away from <dn>Your</dn> eyes. Would <dn>I</dn> ever look again toward <dn>Your</dn> set-apart Hěḵal?’</dq> [5] <dq>Waters encompassed me, unto life, the deep closed around me, weeds were wrapped around my head.</dq> [6] <dq>I went down to the base of the mountains, the earth with its bars were behind me forever. But <dn>You</dn> brought up my life from the pit, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, my <dn>Elohim</dn>.</dq> [7] <dq>When my life fainted within me, <dn>I</dn> remembered <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And my prayer went up to <dn>You</dn>, into <dn>Your</dn> set-apart Hěḵal.</dq> [8] <dq>Those observing false worthlessnesses forsake their own loving-commitment.</dq> [9] <dq>But <dn>I</dn> slaughter to <dn>You</dn> with the voice of thanksgiving, <dn>I</dn> pay what <dn>I</dn> have vowed. Deliverance is of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq>

readings.title: Deliverance onto Dry Land
readings.subtitle: The Fish Obeys the Command
readings.text: [10] Then <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to the fish, and it vomited Yonah onto the dry land.

readings.title: The Second Call
readings.subtitle: Yonah Proclaims the Overthrow of Ninevěh
readings.text: [Jonah 3:1] And the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to Yonah the second time, saying, [2] <dq>Arise, go to Ninevěh, that great city, and proclaim to it <dn>את</dn> the message that <dn>I</dn> am speaking to you.</dq> [3] And Yonah arose and went to Ninevěh, according to the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. Now Ninevěh was a great city before <dn>Elohim</dn>, of three day’s journey. [4] And Yonah began to go in to the city on the first day’s walk. And he cried out and said, “Yet forty days, and Ninevěh shall be overthrown!”

readings.title: The Fast of Repentance
readings.subtitle: A City Turns from Its Violent Hands
readings.text: [5] And the men of Ninevěh believed in <dn>Elohim</dn>, and proclaimed a fast, and put on sackcloth, from the greatest to the least of them. [6] And the word reached the sovereign of Ninevěh, so he arose from his throne and took off his robe, and covered himself with sackcloth and sat in ashes. [7] And he proclaimed and said throughout Ninevěh, “By decree of the sovereign and his nobles: No man or beast, herd or flock, shall taste whatever – let them not eat, let them not even drink water. [8] “But let man and beast be covered with sackcloth, and call mightily to <dn>Elohim</dn>. And let each one turn from his evil way and from the violence that is in his hands. [9] “Who knows whether <dn>Elohim</dn> does turn and relent, and shall turn away from the heat of <dn>His</dn> displeasure, so that we do not perish?”

readings.title: The Relenting of Elohim
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH Witnesses Their Works
readings.text: [10] And <dn>Elohim</dn> saw <dn>את</dn> their works, that they turned from their evil way. And <dn>Elohim</dn> relented from the evil which <dn>He</dn> had said <dn>He</dn> would do to them, and <dn>He</dn> did not do it.

readings.title: The Displeasure of Yonah
readings.subtitle: A Prophet's Frustration with Divine Compassion
readings.text: [Jonah 4:1] But it greatly displeased Yonah, and he was grieved. [2] And he prayed to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and he said, <dq>Please, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, was this not what <dn>I</dn> said while <dn>I</dn> was in my own land? This is why <dn>I</dn> went ahead and fled to Tarshish. For <dn>I</dn> know that <dn>You</dn> are an <dn>Ěl</dn> showing favour, and compassionate, patient and of great loving-commitment, and relenting from doing evil.</dq> [3] <dq>And now, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, please take <dn>את</dn> my life from me, for it is better for me to die than to live!</dq> [4] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said, <dq>Are you right to be displeased?</dq>

readings.title: The Plant and the Scorching Wind
readings.subtitle: An Object Lesson in the Shade
readings.text: [5] Then Yonah went out of the city and sat on the east side of the city, and made himself a shelter there, and sat under it in the shade, to see what would become of the city. [6] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> appointed a plant and made it come up over Yonah, to be a shade for his head to deliver him from his discomfort. And Yonah greatly rejoiced over the plant. [7] But as morning dawned the next day <dn>Elohim</dn> appointed a worm which struck the plant so that it withered. [8] And it came to be when the sun came up, that <dn>Elohim</dn> appointed a scorching east wind, and the sun struck on Yonah’s head, so that he grew faint, and asked for his life to die, and said, “It is better for me to die than to live.”

readings.title: The Masterclass in Compassion
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH’s Sovereign Choice in Premial Deliverance
readings.text: [9] And <dn>Elohim</dn> said to Yonah, <dq>Have you rightly become displeased over the plant?</dq> And he said, “I have rightly become displeased, even to death!” [10] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said, <dq>You felt sorry for the plant for which you have not laboured, nor made it grow, which came up in a night and perished in a night.</dq> [11] <dq>And should <dn>I</dn> not pardon Ninevěh, that great city, in which are more than one hundred and twenty thousand beings who have not known their right hand from their left, and much cattle?</dq>
